questions.question: Which of the following peninsular rivers flows westwards into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapi rivers flow through rift valleys westwards and empty into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: The Kaveri river originates at Talakaveri located in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri river originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri range of the Western Ghats in Kodagu, Karnataka.

questions.question: Tamil Nadu receives the majority of its annual rainfall during which monsoon season?

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the River Cauvery:
I. It originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri Hills of the Western Ghats in Karnataka.
II. The river bifurcates into two branches called Coleroon and Cauvery at the Upper Anaicut (Mukkombu).
III. Hogenakkal Falls is located where the river enters the Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu.
IV. Bhavani, Noyyal, and Amaravathi are major right-bank tributaries of Cauvery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are accurate geographical facts regarding the Cauvery river basin and its drainage course across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
Match List-I (Biosphere Reserves / Sanctuaries in Tamil Nadu) with List-II (Districts / Key Features):
List-I:
(a) Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere
(b) Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary
(c) Mudumalai National Park
(d) Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
List-II:
1. Nilgiris district (Elephant & Tiger habitat)
2. Tirunelveli district (Agasthyamalai biome)
3. Ramanathapuram & Thoothukudi (Coral reefs and Dugong)
4. Nagapattinam district (Migratory waterbirds)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
(a) - (b) - (c) - (d)
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar (Coral/Dugong), Point Calimere (Nagapattinam migratory birds), Mudumalai (Nilgiris), KMTR (Tirunelveli Agasthyamalai).

questions.question:
Assertion [A]: Tamil Nadu receives the bulk of its annual rainfall during the North-East Monsoon season (October to December).
Reason [R]: The Western Ghats act as a topographical barrier to the South-West Monsoon winds, placing most of Tamil Nadu in a rain shadow region during June-September.
Select the correct answer:
options: Both [A] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [A]
Both [A] and [R] are true, but [R] is NOT the correct explanation of [A]
questions.explanation: Because Tamil Nadu lies on the leeward (rain shadow) side of the Western Ghats during the SW monsoon, it depends on retreating NE monsoon winds which pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding soil types in Tamil Nadu:
I. Black soil (Regur) is rich in montmorillonite clay and exhibits self-ploughing characteristics upon drying.
II. Red soil covers the largest geographical area in Tamil Nadu, derived from weathered crystalline metamorphic rocks.
III. Laterite soil is predominantly found in parts of Nilgiris, Salem, and Thanjavur formed by intense leaching.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly characterize the soil taxonomy and geographical distribution across Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:

(b) Nathu La Pass
(c) Palghat (Palakkad) Gap
(d) Bhor Ghat
List-II:
1. Sikkim with Tibet (China)
2. Srinagar with Leh / Ladakh
3. Mumbai with Pune
4. Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) with Palakkad (Kerala)

questions.explanation: Zojila connects Srinagar-Leh; Nathu La connects Sikkim-Tibet; Palghat gap connects Coimbatore-Palakkad; Bhor Ghat links Mumbai-Pune.
